threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it Dalston Junction instead of just ‘the Junction’ while you avoid the east-side row between coffee shops.
Saw a bloke arguing with a bus driver about whether the 36 stops at the old bingo hall—almost missed my stop thanks to their shouting!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard my neighbor's cat yowling during the U-Bahn strike, I realized this place has its own rhythm, even when everything else stops.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find graffiti on the walls of old bakeries next to fresh-baked pastries. It's a sweet, rebellious blend of history and hipster.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how deftly they navigate the BART delays, even making plans based on the time it takes to wait for a train or bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon casually hop onto the bus, strutting down the aisle like it owned the place. No one even flinched; it's just another day in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss the subtle sound of Gràcia’s cobblestones at dawn; it’s like the neighborhood whispers its secrets before the chaos starts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still squint at the sun while standing under the awnings, holding an ice cream like it’s a rare gem.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know someone’s new when they still say 'the tube' instead of 'the Overground' and look lost at Dalston Junction.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in a suit arguing passionately with a street artist about the meaning of life on the 133 last night. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw a guy in a onesie negotiating with a street vendor for a kebab at 3 a.m. on Sonnenallee.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's common to see people drinking beer on park benches while discussing philosophy. No one bats an eye; just typical Berliner life.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they avoid the BART on Fridays, armed with their favorite taco spot’s exact hours instead.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo giving a heartfelt speech to the 38 Geary riders about love while we all just waited in the rain. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just all bohemian bars, but they miss the families who’ve been here for generations, still shopping at the same little shops.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still stare at the metro map like it’s an ancient scroll. Locals just know to follow the crowd.
